name: The St. Regis Rome
positioning: Historic palazzo hotel in central Rome, introduced in 1894 and the first St. Regis in Europe, overlooking Piazza della Repubblica
best_for: Travelers who want a historic base within walking distance of the Trevi Fountain and the Spanish Steps
Guests drawn to art, frescoed interiors and evening cocktail rituals

facts.text: The St. Regis Rome was introduced to society in 1894 and is set in a historic palazzo.
The St. Regis Rome was the first St. Regis in Europe.
The Ritz Ballroom was designed by Roman architect Giulio Podesti and decorated with frescoes by Mario Spinetti.
Mario Spinetti's frescoes in the Ritz Ballroom are protected by the Belle Arti.
Interior design firm Pierre-Yves Rochon oversaw the hotel's makeover.
Guest rooms and suites are styled with Rubelli fabrics, handmade glass and collectable curios.
Bathrooms have Marquina black marble tubs and Acqua di Parma toiletries.
Lumen is the hotel's all-day Italian restaurant, serving breakfast, lunch, aperitif and dinner.
At Lumen, many Italian classics are served from the trolley or finished tableside.
The spa is The St. Regis Rome Spa, Sisley Paris.
The hotel overlooks Piazza della Repubblica and the Diocletian Baths.
The Trevi Fountain and the Spanish Steps are within walking distance.

highlights.text: The Ritz Ballroom was introduced in 1894 as the first public ballroom in Rome.
The lobby has a dove-grey entrance foyer and a 5-metre hand-blown glass chandelier.
Every evening, a champagne sabering ritual takes place at Lumen.
The hotel's version of the St. Regis Bloody Mary is the Red Admiral, made with all-Italian spices and flavors.
In January 2020, Galleria Continua opened a permanent exhibition space at the hotel.

considerations.text: Lumen Garden is a seasonal outlet, open from May to September and reserved for private receptions.
Small balconies or terraces are limited to specific suites.
WhataHotel notes ultra-luxury pricing that reflects the premium positioning.
